name: Minnesota

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt from state and local sales taxes; candy, soft drinks, dietary supplements and prepared food are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.
Alcohol bought in stores: 6.875% sales tax plus the 2.5% liquor gross receipts tax.
Drinks served pay the 6.875% sales tax plus the 2.5% liquor gross receipts tax, like bottles bought in stores.

Cigarettes aren't subject to the sales tax: a cigarette sales tax in lieu of it (84.0 cents a pack in 2026, 87.7 cents from January 1, 2027), close to the state rate, is paid at wholesale, and no local sales tax applies to them; other tobacco and e-cigarettes pay the state and local sales tax on top of a 95% wholesale tax. The state rate is used for the whole category and local tax is left out.
Household supplies: diapers are exempt from state and local sales tax, which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: feminine hygiene products are exempt, which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services aren't taxed; massage and tanning are, which is not counted here.

Clothing is exempt, but not clothing accessories: jewelry and watches are taxed at 6.875% and counted on their share of US sales of clothing, shoes and jewelry (13%, 2022 Economic Census), 0.89% of what is spent on clothing, shoes and jewelry; the category's rate also takes in laundry and dry cleaning, at their own rate. Other accessories, fur clothing and sports or protective equipment are taxed too but not counted, since no official figure gives their share, nor are local taxes on jewelry.
Laundry and dry cleaning: taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead: 32.6 cents in 2026, left out here.
Auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).
A 50-cent retail delivery fee applies to taxable deliveries of $100 or more, which is not counted here.

Lodging pays local lodging taxes in many cities (Minneapolis 3% plus 3% downtown, St. Paul 3% or 7% by size, Rochester and Bloomington 7%, Duluth 3% plus 2.5% for larger hotels, and others), which are not counted here.
gaps: Local rate in each city is the most common combination among its ZIP+4 records (county, city and special taxing district taxes such as the metro-area transportation and housing taxes).
Lodging, entertainment and other special local taxes are not included; food and beverage taxes are, where each city's notes say so.

Meeker County's 0.5% transit tax and the St. Cloud Area's 0.5% (St. Cloud, Sartell, Sauk Rapids, St. Joseph and St. Augusta) are coded in the Streamlined Sales Tax boundary file without a county or city, so they are added here from the Department of Revenue's rate guide. Food and beverage taxes of Detroit Lakes, Marshall, Proctor, Mankato, North Mankato, St. Cloud and Duluth are counted in their restaurant rates; Minneapolis's downtown, Bloomington's and Giants Ridge's taxes are noted on those pages.

2706616: Bloomington adds 3% on on-sale liquor and 3% on admissions and recreation (City of Bloomington); they aren't counted here.
2715832: Detroit Lakes' 1% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
2717000: Duluth's 2.25% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (City of Duluth).
2725118: Grand Rapids' 0.5% city sales tax ends December 31, 2026 (Department of Revenue); the current rate is used here.
2739878: Mankato's 0.5% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
2740688: Marshall's 1.5% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
2743000: Minneapolis adds 3% on restaurant food and 3% on on-sale liquor in its downtown taxing area (Department of Revenue); they aren't counted here, since they cover only part of the city and the area isn't mapped.
2747068: North Mankato's 0.5% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
2752630: Proctor's 1% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
2756896: St. Cloud's 1% food and beverage tax on restaurant meals is counted in its restaurant rate (Department of Revenue).
St. Cloud also taxes on-sale liquor at 1% (Department of Revenue), which isn't counted here.
2706148: In the Giants Ridge Recreation Area, a 1% food and beverage tax and a 2% admissions and recreation tax apply (Department of Revenue); they aren't counted here, since the area is only part of the city.
27093: Meeker County's 0.5% transit tax (since July 1, 2026; Department of Revenue) is counted here; the Streamlined Sales Tax boundary file codes it without a county, so it is added from the Department of Revenue's rate guide.
27095: The GKW Sanitary District's 1% sales tax applies in Garrison, Kathio, Roosevelt and Hazelton townships and part of Mille Lacs County (Department of Revenue); it isn't counted in the county's rate here.
2703070: Avon is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2711800: Clearwater is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2728394: Henderson is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2741426: Medford is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2750470: Perham is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2758648: Sauk Centre is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2761690: Spicer is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.
2767792: Walker is less than half of each census tract it is in, so the figures here use the surrounding area's rates for its tract, not its own.

warn: County Business Patterns counts 4 liquor stores with 51 jobs in Grant County (2023), but the 2022 Economic Census counted 35 jobs in all its food and beverage stores together, and the Minnesota Department of Revenue put the taxable sales of all its food and beverage stores at $6.0 million in 2024. The model gives its liquor stores about $8 million, so Grant County's alcohol store sales and retention rate are likely too high.

Murray County's two municipal liquor stores (Avoca and Hadley) sold $583,549 in 2024 (Minnesota State Auditor), and the Minnesota Department of Revenue put the taxable sales of all its food and beverage stores at $4.5 million in 2024. The model gives its liquor stores about $8 million (its other four liquor stores in County Business Patterns, each at the average sales of a private liquor store in Minnesota's small counties), so Murray County's alcohol store sales and retention rate are likely too high.
